findings.text: follow-on (persisted from the prior two reviews): plan §3's done-when has three clauses and the evidence fragment still carries none of the measured ones. §3 requires 'a cold fetch of one OP2 shot's first-pass signals completes through the extractor in a single ssh session; a warm read of the same signals through the view touches no network; and the extractor's wall time per signal and bytes per signal are recorded in the evidence so the cache for a shot set is sized rather than guessed.' The single-session and no-network-on-warm-read properties are asserted against a fake transport (legitimate for a unit gate), but the wall-time-per-signal and bytes-per-signal measurement is still absent and no real cold fetch was run (the ssh link to IFERC is down, §5). The delta did not attempt this clause; it remains the section's outstanding measured deliverable.

follow-on (integration seam, read/write asymmetry): the recorded EDDB token is consulted only on the write path. normalised_shot/channel_path alias every series token with the same digits to the same integer directory, so once a channel exists under one token, a read through a different series token silently resolves to it: is_cached(root, 'C101173', 'MMSYS', 'CS1') returns True against a store written under 'E101173'. The node's own test_a_second_token_sharing_the_digits_is_refused asserts exactly this (is_cached(tmp_path, 'C101173', 'MMSYS', 'CS1') is True) after writing 'E101173'. §3 requires only that a *write* with a differing token be refused, so the write contract is met, but the read path offers no equivalent guard and read_eddb_token is not consulted by is_cached. A consumer that reads by token rather than by integer can receive another series' data without a refusal. Noted rather than required; the fix would be to compare the requested token against read_eddb_token in the read predicate.

follow-on (edge case, reproduced this review): write_channel opens the pulse group with zarr.open_group(..., mode='a') at line 220, before it validates that the record's own time vector matches its data width at line 238. A record whose time length disagrees with its data width is therefore refused AFTER the group directory has been created, leaving an empty '<int>.zarr' on disk with no eddb_token attribute and no arrays. Reproduced against the head arm (rev 3d2192c8): write_channel(root, Rec('E101173','MMSYS','CS1', zeros((2,5)), arange(3))) raises 'time base length 3 does not match data width 5', and 101173.zarr then exists with read_eddb_token(...) is None. Benign litter - is_cached then returns False and a later correct fetch fills it - but a rejected malformed record should leave no directory behind. The shape check belongs before open_group, or the group should be opened lazily.

follow-on (batch-abort design note): fetch_channels builds its missing list with an up-front is_cached scan, and _channel_present now raises EddbCacheError for a node that exists but does not open as an array. So one corrupt on-disk channel aborts the whole batch before any transport call - the node's own test_an_unreadable_channel_node_is_refused_not_reported_not_cached asserts transport.calls == [] after the raise. Refusing rather than refetching a corrupt node is the intended 'never rewrite measured data' behaviour, but the same scan that produces the refusal also denies every other channel in the batch. A per-request skip of a corrupt node that still refuses it would preserve the good channels. The plan does not settle this; noted, not required.

follow-on (edge case, minor): _TOKEN_RE = r'^(?P<series>[A-Za-z])?(?P<digits>\d+)$' accepts a single optional letter followed by any number of digits, so it does not enforce §3's six-digit form. A token such as 'E10' or '101173123' is accepted and normalised ('10'), and eddb_token('E10') returns 'E10', which would then be recorded as a pulse token. The plan states the EDDB form is a series letter and six digits; validating the digit count at _split_token would refuse a malformed token at the boundary rather than caching it under a truncated integer. Low severity, not reproduced as a failure.

The first fails with 'DID NOT RAISE EddbCacheError' at the overwrite refusal; the second fails because the removed call also carried the corrupt-node refusal, so the corrupt node is then rejected with a different message. The reviewed run's own negative_control.log names the same two ids, so the guard is real and falsifiable.
